Caesar is a desktop API client for Windo: Caesar is a desktop API client for Windows, macOS and Linux. It lets you build, send and test HTTP requests, GraphQL and WebSocket, organize them into collections and share them with your team, all from a clean interface where color and the keyboard save you clicks.
<strong>Local-first:</strong> in Guest m: Local-first: in Guest mode your collections live on your device. It works offline and without an account.
<strong>Truly fast:</strong> it is built: Truly fast: it is built with Rust and Tauri, not a bundled browser.
<strong>Familiar:</strong> if you come f: Familiar: if you come from Postman or Insomnia, you can import your collections and your pm.* scripts keep working.
<strong>Fair Source (FSL):</strong> the: Fair Source (FSL): the code is public and free to use. It is not open source: selling it is prohibited.
<strong>Who is it for?</strong> For anyo: Who is it for? For anyone who tests APIs every day (backend, frontend, QA, mobile) and wants a lightweight, private, frictionless tool. Also for anyone who needs to share collections with their team without setting up infrastructure.
Caesar's speed is not a trick: it comes: Caesar's speed is not a trick: it comes from how it is built.
Rust instead of a bundled browser: Rust instead of a bundled browser
Requests are executed by a Rust core and: Requests are executed by a Rust core and the window uses the web engine that already ships with your system. The result: instant startup and low memory use.
Your data is right next to you: Your data is right next to you
Collections, variables and tabs are read: Collections, variables and tabs are read from your disk, without waiting for any server. Opening Caesar does not depend on your connection.
No mandatory sign-in screen, no telemetr: No mandatory sign-in screen, no telemetry and no analytics running in the background.

Caesar updates itself: on startup it loo: Caesar updates itself: on startup it looks for a new version and, if there is one, downloads it, installs it and restarts. Your tabs and drafts are kept. Every package is signed and the application verifies the signature before installing it.
In <em>Settings → Updates</em> you can t: In Settings → Updates you can turn them off or click Check for updates.
